meta.description: Add a new Regular or Admin user account to the CardDemo system's user security file.
meta.process_description: This program presents a data entry screen to an authorised administrator, allowing them to create a new user account in the CardDemo system. The administrator must supply the new user's first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type (Regular or Admin). Upon submission, the program validates that all fields are populated, checks that the user ID does not already exist, and if all validations pass, writes the new user record to the USRSEC security file. Success or failure feedback is displayed on screen, and duplicate user IDs are explicitly rejected to maintain uniqueness of user accounts.

files.USRSEC: User security file storing all CardDemo user account credentials and access type (Regular/Admin)

business_rules: First Name is mandatory — a new user account cannot be created without a first name.
Last Name is mandatory — a new user account cannot be created without a last name.
User ID is mandatory — a new user account cannot be created without a user ID.
Password is mandatory — a new user account cannot be created without a password.
User Type is mandatory — the access level (Regular or Admin) must be specified for every new user.
User ID must be unique — if the User ID already exists in the USRSEC file, the record is rejected with a 'User ID already exists' error and no duplicate record is written.
Only authenticated and authorised users (administrators) can access this program; unauthenticated sessions are redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C).
Upon successful creation, the entry form is cleared and a confirmation message is displayed, allowing the administrator to add another user immediately.
PF3 navigates back to the Admin menu (COADM01C); PF4 clears the current screen without saving; any other key press is treated as invalid.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group-level container holding all working-storage variables used during the Add User business process, including program identity, error tracking, and file references.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program ('COUSR01C'), used to identify itself when transferring control to other programs or logging activity — essentially the program's own identity card within the CardDemo system.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CU01') associated with the Add User function. This is the transaction code an administrator invokes to launch the new user creation screen, and it is used when navigating back to this program from other screens.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed to the administrator on the screen after an action is taken — for example, confirming that a new user was successfully created, or explaining why the submission was rejected (e.g., 'User ID already exists', missing mandatory field).

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The physical name of the User Security File ('USRSEC') where all CardDemo user account credentials and access types are stored. This is the target file to which a new user record is written upon successful account creation.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator flag that tracks whether any validation or processing problem has occurred during the Add User process. It starts as 'N' (no error) and is set to 'Y' if, for example, a mandatory field is missing or the User ID already exists, preventing the record from being written.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: A named condition that evaluates to true when an error has been detected during the Add User process (e.g., duplicate User ID, missing mandatory field). When active, it signals that the new user record must NOT be written to the security file and the administrator must be shown an error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: A named condition that evaluates to true when no errors have been detected, meaning all mandatory fields are present, the User ID is unique, and the new user account is safe to be written to the security file.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after a file operation (such as writing the new user record to USRSEC or reading to check for a duplicate User ID). A non-zero value indicates that the file operation did not succeed as expected, which the program uses to detect and handle errors such as a duplicate record or file unavailability.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code that provides additional detail about why a file operation failed, complementing the response code. It helps the program distinguish between different failure scenarios (e.g., record already exists vs. file not found) when attempting to add a new user to the security file.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area used to pass session and context information between programs. In the Add User process, it carries details such as the logged-in administrator's identity and user type, allowing the program to verify that the caller is an authenticated administrator before permitting access to the user creation function.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: A placeholder field within the CICS communication area that allows the program to detect whether a communication area was passed when the program was invoked. Its presence or absence (and length) tells the program whether this is a fresh entry from the menu or a return from another screen, determining how the Add User form should be initialised.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph that controls the entire user-add session flow. It determines whether to present the data entry screen, process a submitted form, or redirect the administrator based on their key press or session state.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph enforces all mandatory field validations when an administrator submits a new user creation request, and if all fields are valid, writes the new user account to the security file. It acts as the central gate-keeper ensuring no incomplete or duplicate user records are ever persisted.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles navigation away from the Add User screen, transferring control back to the appropriate previous screen — defaulting to the sign-on screen if no specific destination was recorded. It packages the current transaction's identity into the shared communication area before handing off control.

paragraphs.name: SEND-USRADD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares and displays the Add User data entry screen to the administrator, including any status or error messages resulting from a previous submission attempt. It ensures the screen is fully refreshed with current feedback before awaiting the next administrator input.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-USRADD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the data entered by the administrator on the Add User screen, retrieving all typed field values (first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type) so they can be validated and processed to create the new user account.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the header section of the Add User screen with contextual information — application titles, the active transaction identifier, the program name, and the current date and time — so that the administrator sees a fully labelled and timestamped screen before entering new user details.

paragraphs.name: WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph attempts to permanently save the new user account to the security file and then provides the administrator with immediate feedback — either confirming successful creation, rejecting a duplicate User ID, or reporting an unexpected system failure.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Resets the user account creation form to a blank state, ready for a new entry. This is triggered when an administrator explicitly requests a screen clear (PF4) without saving any data entered.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the user account creation form to a blank state, clearing all previously entered data and any status messages. This is used to prepare the screen for a fresh user account entry, either after a successful creation or when the administrator explicitly clears the form.
